images.title: Shortest route from A to B
images.purpose: Show that of all routes from A to B, the straight one is shortest, the line segment AB.
images.composition: Two points with three routes between them, laid out horizontally with wide spacing.
images.exact_structure: Two dots, A on the left and B on the right, same horizontal level. Between them 3 routes: one curved grey #6B7280 route bending above, one zig-zag grey route below with exactly 3 straight parts, and one straight teal #0072B2 route in the middle. Exactly 2 points, 3 routes, only the straight one coloured.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
routes drawn with unequal end points
images.takeaway: The straight route from A to B is the shortest.
images.description: Points A and B joined by a curved grey route, a zig-zag grey route and a straight teal route, with the straight one marked shortest.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to trace each route with a finger and say which is shortest.

image_decisions.why: The idea is a picture idea; one clean image carries it.
